battle.name: 第一次伊利里亞戰爭
battle.theater: 亞得里亞海東岸與科基拉海峽
battle.brief: 公元前229年伊利里亞攝政女王特歐塔劫掠羅馬商船、殺死使者，羅馬翌年派兩軍團渡海討伐，在科基拉海戰破敵、於杜勒斯夜襲登陸，攻取法拉斯島逼出求和。卡面之埃及月牙劍非本役實物：這把公元前1500年的鐮形單刃劍在埃及已式微，它所屬的鐮形劍族在伊利里亞戰士手中以 falcata 延續。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 公元前229至前228年的第一次伊利里亞戰爭，交戰的兩邊是羅馬共和國與伊利里亞王國（阿爾迪亞伊王朝），但兩方的國家形式相差極遠。羅馬是由元老院與人民會議共同授權的共和政體，開戰與媾和都經過議決，戰場指揮由兩名執政官分擔：公元前229年，執政官弗爾維烏斯·森圖馬盧斯率二十五艘戰艦東進；公元前228年，執政官普布利烏斯·尤尼烏斯·布魯圖斯率主力渡海。羅馬的骨幹是公民兵團，每團約四千二百名步兵與三百名騎兵，其餘兵員由同盟與外族補足：埃托利亞聯盟、亞該亞聯盟、帕加馬王國、埃庇魯斯同盟各出步兵，合計約兩萬步兵、兩千騎兵；科基拉城邦在遭伊利里亞人攻擊後正式加入羅馬同盟。伊利里亞一方則是阿格龍王創建的阿爾迪亞伊王國，以斯庫德拉為核心，控制亞得里亞海東岸自伊斯特拉半島至諾曼一線，另有伊薩（維斯）、法拉斯的自治或附庸城市，港口與島嶼構成其海運命脈。特歐塔女王以攝政身份掌國，兒子庇涅斯年幼，實權集中於女王與少數首領手中；命令體系帶有強烈的首長色彩，沿海各城與海軍指揮官各自為戰，號令不統一；王國有常備步卒與數量可觀的小型快船，卻沒有羅馬式的糧秣與兵員補充體系。以上差距，正是這場戰爭在兩三個月內見分曉的根本原因。
countriesEn: From 229 to 228 BC the First Illyrian War was fought between the Roman Republic and the kingdom of Illyria under the Ardiaean dynasty, though the two states were separated by a very long way in the forms they took. Rome was a republic in which the Senate and the popular assembly shared the authority to declare war and to make peace, and the field command was divided between two consuls: in 229 BC Gnaeus Fulvius Centumalus sailed east with twenty-five warships, and in 228 BC Publius Junius Brutus took the main body across the sea. The backbone of the Roman force was the citizen legion, each of about four thousand two hundred infantry and three hundred cavalry, with the numbers made up by allies and foreigners: the Aetolian League, the Achaean League, the kingdom of Pergamon and the Epirote League between them furnished about twenty thousand foot and two thousand horse. The city of Corcyra, after being attacked by the Illyrians, was formally taken into the Roman alliance. On the other side stood the kingdom of Illyria founded by King Agron, with Scodra as its core, holding the eastern shore of the Adriatic from the Istrian peninsula as far as the Bay of Kotor, with Issa (Vis) and Pharos in dependent or subject condition; the harbours and islands of that coast were the sea lifeline of the state. Queen Teuta held power as regent for her young son Pinnes, and real authority was concentrated in the queen and a handful of chiefs; the chain of command carried a strong personal character, the coastal towns and the naval commanders each acted on their own initiative, and orders were not consistently transmitted. The kingdom had standing infantry and a considerable number of small fast ships, but no Roman-style supply system and no means of replacing losses. That gap is the underlying reason the whole affair was settled within two or three months.
people: 關鍵人物集中在少數人身上。伊利里亞方面，國王阿格龍在公元前229年率軍支援埃托利亞聯盟、進攻亞該亞聯盟控制的地區時負傷，隨即去世；他留下未成年的兒子庇涅斯，由妻子特歐塔攝政。女王特歐塔在史料中以「海妖」形象流傳——這是敵意宣傳的產物，但她在關鍵決定上並非傀儡：商船被劫之後她索要高昂贖金，兩名羅馬使者到場時，依據波里比烏斯的記載，其中一人被她兄弟克蘭尼烏斯殺害，另一人受辱而返，特歐塔隨即拒絕和談，把一場贖金糾紛升級為全面戰爭。法拉斯的海軍首領德米特里奧斯是全場最識時務的人：公元前228年羅馬兵臨法拉斯時，他沒有抵抗，反而率眾投向羅馬，被待為上賓並獲准繼續統治法拉斯；此舉為羅馬打開了東岸的灘頭，也直接造成伊利里亞內部的裂痕。羅馬方面，執政官布魯圖斯是此役的主腦：他在科基拉把全軍分為兩路，一路隨艦隊封鎖島嶼與港口，一路沿海岸強推，最終迫使對方求和；隨軍使者中還有元老院派來的人，其報告是元老院批准用兵的依據。科基拉的居民代表也親赴羅馬陳情，說明伊利里亞人的劫掠如何逼近他們的城牆，羅馬介入的直接理由由此成形。史家波里比烏斯本人是伊利里亞人，家族受過伊利里亞方面的傷害，他記錄此役時立場鮮明，但關於兵力、俘獲與行程的細節仍是今日重建戰役的主要依據。
peopleEn: A handful of people carry the campaign. On the Illyrian side, King Agron was wounded in 229 BC while leading an expedition to support the Aetolian League against territory held by the Achaean League, and died soon afterwards; he left a small child, Pinnes, and his wife Teuta took over as regent. Teuta survives in the sources as a siren figure, and that image is the product of hostile propaganda, but she was no puppet where decisions counted: after the merchant ship was plundered she demanded a high ransom, and when the two Roman envoys arrived, one of them was killed — Polybius names her brother Cranius as the man who did it — while the other was insulted and sent home; Teuta then refused any settlement and turned a ransom dispute into a full-scale war. The most astute man in the story was Demetrius of Pharos, the naval commander there: when the Romans came up against Pharos in 228 BC he did not resist but came over to them with his men, was treated as a guest of honour and was allowed to continue ruling the island; that move gave Rome its bridgehead on the eastern shore and split the Illyrian command in two. On the Roman side the brain of the operation was the consul Brutus: at Corcyra he split the whole army into two columns, one sailing with the fleet to blockade the islands and harbours and one pressing forward along the coast under his own hand, until the enemy was driven to ask for terms. Among the envoys who accompanied the army were men sent by the Senate, and their report was the basis on which the Senate approved the use of force. Representatives from Corcyra also came to Rome in person to set out how the Illyrian raids were closing in on their walls, and the immediate reason for Roman intervention was shaped by that petition. The historian Polybius was himself an Illyrian, and his family had suffered at Illyrian hands; the bias in his account of this war is obvious, but his details of numbers, captures and distances remain the principal basis for reconstructing the campaign today.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是埃及月牙劍，約公元前1500年定型：外彎的單刃，刃形如柳葉，握柄貼近刀背，砍入之後不必拔刀再揮，設計原為對付北美及非洲的皮甲與網盾。必須說清楚的是，公元前229年時它在埃及本國已退居末流——軍中更常見的是科普什（kopis）那樣更長更直的弧刃單手劍與雙刃直劍，月牙劍只剩下儀仗、衛護與老兵懷中的殘留位置，因此它並不是本役的實物。但同一個鐮形劍家族在亞得里亞海東岸正當盛時：伊利里亞與達爾馬提亞的戰士使用 falcata，一種刃身近乎直、只在近柄處微彎、尖端收成窄尖的單刃劍，砍劈兼具刺擊之便，正是卡面月牙劍在伊利里亞軍中最直接的親屬。伊利里亞的裝備體系另有幾個特徵：步兵以輕裝為主，用小圓盾（parma）、短矛、投槍與標槍，不穿希臘式重甲，靠速度與地形取勝；海軍的核心是 liburna 這類單列槳快船，船身狹長、划行極快，專門用來追擊羅馬的運輸船隊，船上有標槍手與鉤索手，專攻對方船欄。羅馬方面的裝備則完全是另一套：執政官旗下是每團約四千二百人的公民步兵，配大方盾、加重標槍與短劍，另有數百人編成的騎兵小隊；海上用三列槳與五列槳戰列船，岸上備有投石機、弩炮、攻城塔與可拆裝的浮橋；隨軍的百艘貨船把義大利的糧食、鐵器與攻城器械運過海，同盟的埃托利亞與亞該亞供應糧秣，帕加馬則提供海運與經驗。交通方面，羅馬沿阿波羅尼亞、埃庇丹努斯、利蘇斯一線的沿海道路推進，隊伍靠每日挖壕紮營的軍營制度宿營。歸納而言：卡面月牙劍代表的是這一系武器的最早形態，而它真正在公元前229年還活著的後裔，是伊利里亞戰士手裡那把 falcata。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh, a form that took shape around 1500 BC: a single blade with the edge on the outside, the profile of a willow leaf and the grip set close to the back of the blade, designed so that a blow could be followed by another without pulling the sword free. It has to be said plainly that by 229 BC the weapon was already a backwater in Egypt itself — what the armies actually carried was the kopis, a longer and straighter curved single-hander, or the straight double-edged sword, while the khopesh survived only in ceremony, in bodyguard duty and in the memory of old soldiers. It was therefore not an actual weapon in this campaign. The same family of sickled blades, however, was in its prime on the eastern Adriatic: Illyrian and Dalmatian warriors carried the falcata, a single-edged sword whose blade is almost straight, curving only near the hilt and tapering to a narrow point, at once a chopping and a thrusting weapon, and the closest relative on the battlefield of the khopesh shown on the card. Illyrian equipment had other characteristics of its own: the infantry were light, armed with the small round parma shield, short spears, javelins and throwing darts, wearing no Greek-style heavy armour, and winning by speed and by the ground they chose. The heart of their navy was the liburna, a light galley with a single bank of oars, narrow of beam and very fast under the oars, built to run down Roman transport hulls, with javelin men and hook-handlers aboard to work at the enemy's rail. Roman equipment belonged to an entirely different order: under the consuls were citizen infantry of about four thousand two hundred to a legion, with the large scutum, the heavy pilum and the short sword, plus cavalry units of a few hundred men; at sea they used triremes and quinqueremes, on land stone-throwers, cheiroballistae, siege towers and dismantlable pontoon bridges; a hundred merchant ships carried grain, iron and siege equipment across from Italy, with grain supplied by the Aetolians and Achaeans and shipping capacity by Pergamon. In transport terms, the Romans advanced along the coastal road running through Apollonia, Epidamnus and Lissus, and the column bivouacked by the system of the camp, with a ditch dug every evening. To sum it up: the khopesh on the card stands at the earliest end of this line of weapons, and the form of it that was still alive in 229 BC was the falcata in the hands of the Illyrian warrior.
tactics: 這場戰爭可以分成三段戰術課本。科基拉海面一役，羅馬二十五艘戰艦面對數量更多的伊利里亞快船，羅馬人不求全速追擊，而是收成緊密隊形，以船首撞角與甲板接舷戰取勝；海戰的勝負不在撞擊，而在登船後甲板上的步戰與投射武器密度——這正是羅馬人熟悉的領域。陸戰部分，執政官布魯圖斯在抵達科基拉後把全軍分為兩路：一路隨艦隊駛向法拉斯、接管島上要塞；一路由他本人率領，沿亞得里亞海東岸狹窄的沿海平原推進，前哨是盟邦埃庇魯斯的阿波羅尼亞，最遠據點是埃庇丹努斯。伊利里亞軍在杜勒斯一帶的營地於黎明時被羅馬軍襲擊，營中缺乏壕溝與柵牆，士兵未及集結即被壓垮，羅馬騎兵隨即在沿海平地追擊潰兵。奪港之後的作戰，羅馬沒有強攻斯庫德拉——那是建在河流匯合處、有三重城牆的堅城，強攻而無攻城塔與圍城器具必遭挫敗——而是轉而沿海岸掃蕩、佔領伊薩與法拉斯，切斷伊利里亞的海上收入，再用封鎖代替攻城，把壓力轉給對方的執政層。整體而言，羅馬的戰術是「海陸並行、封鎖消耗、避免攻堅」：以騎兵偵察前路、以海軍切斷糧道、以兩萬同盟軍的兵力擺出包圍的樣子，最後以談判收兵；而伊利里亞的戰術是「海盜式游擊加據點固守」，靠速度與熟悉海峽彌補兵力差距，卻始終無法把分散的小船與據點連成一條防線。補給是這一役的關鍵變量：羅馬的糧食全靠海運，一旦護衛艦被牽制在科基拉，運輸船隊就會暴露在快船面前，這也是雙方開戰首月爭奪的真正目標。
tacticsEn: This war can be read as three tactical lessons. In the action off Corcyra the twenty-five Roman warships faced a numerically larger fleet of Illyrian fast ships; the Romans did not try to chase at full speed but drew into a close order and fought with the ram and with boarding, and the decision was not made by the impact but by the density of missile fire and hand-to-hand fighting on the decks, which was the Romans' own ground. On land, once the army reached Corcyra the consul Brutus split it in two: one column went with the fleet to Pharos and took over the island's strongholds, the other marched under his own command along the narrow coastal strip of the eastern Adriatic, with Apollonia in friendly Epirus as the forward post and Epidamnus as the furthest point. The Illyrian camp near Dyrrhachium was attacked by the Romans at daybreak; with no ditch and no palisade, the Illyrians were overrun before they could form, and the Roman horse pursued the fugitives across the flat coastal ground. Having taken the harbour, the Romans did not assault Scodra — a fortress of three walls standing at the confluence of two rivers, which without towers and siege gear would certainly have cost them dearly — but turned instead to sweep the coast, occupy Issa and Pharos, cut the Illyrian maritime revenue, and let blockade take the place of assault, so that the pressure fell on the Illyrian governing council. The Roman method was parallelism at sea and on land, blockade and attrition, and the avoidance of pointless assaults: cavalry scouted the road ahead, the fleet cut the supply line, the twenty thousand allied infantry were displayed to suggest encirclement, and the business was finished by negotiation. The Illyrian method was piratical harassment combined with the defence of fixed points, using speed and intimate knowledge of the straits to make up for the difference in numbers, yet never able to join their scattered boats and strongholds into a single line of defence. Supply was the decisive variable of the campaign: Roman grain moved entirely by water, and the moment the escorting warships were held up off Corcyra the transport fleet was exposed to the fast boats, which is why the first weeks of the war were fought over the convoy rather than over the town.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰爭跨公元前229與前228兩個年度，主要戰鬥集中在公元前228年夏秋。兵力方面，據波里比烏斯記載，羅馬投入兩軍團，每團約四千二百名步兵、三百名騎兵，合計約八千四百步兵、六百騎兵；同盟方面約二萬步兵、二千騎兵。船隊方面，一百艘貨船負責運載軍隊與糧秣，另有約二十艘三列槳戰艦護航；駐科基拉的先遣艦隊為二十五艘戰艦，與之交戰的伊利里亞船隊數量更多，約五十艘。行程上，自義大利越亞得里亞海至科基拉歷時數日，沿海自阿波羅尼亞至埃庇丹努斯約數十公里，全程仍在羅馬同盟的補給圈內。戰利品方面，羅馬在利蘇斯一帶奪得伊利里亞人泊岸的戰船約八十艘，並取得斯庫德拉一帶銀礦的礦石與白銀。戰俘與投降方面，法拉斯的德米特里奧斯率眾歸附並被護送回羅馬；和談中伊利里亞方面被要求交出人質。需注意這些數字多出自波里比烏斯一人的記載，古代戰報與遠征記述常有誇張，兵員與船數應作概數看，俘獲船隻的數目尤須保留餘地。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war straddled the two years 229 and 228 BC, with the main operations concentrated in the summer and autumn of 228. In strength, Polybius records two Roman legions of about four thousand two hundred infantry and three hundred cavalry each, roughly eight thousand four hundred foot and six hundred horse in all; the allies contributed about twenty thousand foot and two thousand horse. On the naval side, a hundred merchant ships carried the army and its baggage, with about twenty triremes as escort; the advance squadron at Corcyra was twenty-five warships, and the Illyrian fleet it engaged was larger, about fifty ships. In distance, the crossing from Italy across the Adriatic to Corcyra took a number of days, and the coastal march from Apollonia to Epidamnus was a few tens of kilometres, the whole operation staying inside the supply ring of Rome's allies. In captures, the Romans took on the coast at Lissus about eighty Illyrian vessels found beached, together with ore and silver from the mines near Scodra. In surrenders, Demetrius of Pharos came over with his men and was escorted to Rome; in the settlement the Illyrians were required to give hostages. These numbers rest for the most part on the testimony of a single author, Polybius, and ancient despatches and descriptions of expeditions tend to inflate; the figures for men and ships should be read as approximations, and the count of captured vessels especially should be treated with reserve.
cause: 開戰的起因疊了三層。最外層是商路上的摩擦：公元前3世紀末，義大利南部與西西里商人把亞得里亞海當作前往東方的高利潤航線，羅馬公民船隻駛入伊利里亞人控制的海域愈來愈多，衝突隨之增加。公元前229年夏，一艘載著糧食的羅馬商船在法拉斯附近失事或遭襲，船員被伊利里亞人殺害並劫走貨物；特歐塔提出的解決辦法是要羅馬付贖金贖回殘骸與倖存者，羅馬方面認為這是海盜式的勒索，拒絕付款。接著而來的是使者被殺：羅馬派去的兩名使者中一人被殺，另一人受辱返回，消息送回羅馬，輿論立刻把這件事定性為國家冒犯——對一個以護商與榮譽自命的共和政體而言，使者被殺是不能容忍的技術性事故。深層原因是伊利里亞方面的王權重組：阿格龍一死，攝政的特歐塔既要穩住內部、又要維持王國的財政收入，劫掠航運是最來得快的方法；羅馬在科基拉建立同盟、又在亞得里亞海立威，則直接威脅到她對沿海的壟斷。還有第三層——羅馬的戰略需求：剛打完第二次布匿戰爭的羅馬需要新的戰場與戰利品，東方的希臘世界正因埃托利亞與亞該亞的衝突而混亂，介入亞得里亞海既能拿到錢，又能讓羅馬以「援助盟友」的名義出現在希臘人的地盤上。三層疊加，才使一次商船糾紛變成了兩軍團渡海的遠征。
causeEn: The outbreak stacked three layers of cause. The outermost was friction on the trading route: in the last decades of the 3rd century BC, merchants from southern Italy and Sicily were using the Adriatic as the high-profit road to the East, and Roman citizen ships entered Illyrian-controlled waters more and more often, so the collisions multiplied. In the summer of 229 BC a Roman merchantman carrying grain was lost or attacked off Pharos, her crew killed by Illyrians and her cargo taken; the solution Teuta proposed was that Rome should pay a ransom for the wreck and the survivors, and the Roman side regarded this as pirate blackmail and refused to pay. Next came the murder of the envoys: of the two men Rome sent, one was killed and the other was sent back insulted; the news reached Rome and opinion at once treated it as an act against the state, and for a republic that made a virtue of protecting commerce and good name, the killing of envoys was an intolerable technicality. The deeper cause lay in the reorganisation of Illyrian kingship: after Agron's death the regent Teuta had to hold the state together and keep its revenue coming, and taking the shipping was the fastest way to do it; Rome's alliance with Corcyra and its standing in the Adriatic threatened her monopoly of the coast directly. There was a third layer as well, Roman strategic need: a Rome fresh from the Second Punic War wanted a new theatre and a new source of booty, the Greek world was already confused by the quarrels of the Aetolian and Achaean leagues, and intervening in the Adriatic would bring money while letting Rome appear in Greek lands under the respectable title of helper of allies. Only the three layers together turned a quarrel about a ship into a two-legion expedition across the sea.
impact: 這場戰爭的餘波比戰役本身長得多。對伊利里亞王國而言，法拉斯島的易主等於王國在亞得里亞海東岸的海上支柱被抽走，首都斯庫德拉雖然暫時未破，卻已失去外海的屏障；公元前219年，第二次伊利里亞戰爭中羅馬攻陷斯庫德拉與里松，阿爾迪亞伊王國才真正覆亡，原有城邦隨之各自尋找新的靠山，達爾馬提亞的達奧爾西人與後來的根提烏斯相繼崛起。對羅馬而言，這是第一次走出義大利，把海軍推進到亞得里亞海，並且第一次以同盟體系作戰：埃托利亞、亞該亞、帕加馬的步兵與糧秣證明羅馬可以靠聯盟打大規模戰爭，而不必讓公民兵單獨承擔；科基拉、杜勒斯一線的停戰與伊薩、法拉斯的據點，則讓羅馬在巴爾干西岸有了以後可以依賴的落腳點，此後第三次馬其頓戰爭與公元前2世紀的希臘戰爭都建立在這條通道上。經濟上，伊利里亞的白銀與造船木材從此源源流向羅馬，成為羅馬在義大利、西西里與希臘作戰的重要支撐。思想上，此役是有記載以來第一場由羅馬人自己記錄下來的戰爭——史家波里比烏斯以它作為《歷史》全書的起點，最早的羅馬史著作《六章本》由此而生；波里比烏斯本人是伊利里亞人，他記下的不只是一場戰爭，也是一部家族記憶裡的世仇。最後是海軍技術的傳遞：伊利里亞人的快船在戰後被羅馬人吸收，成為羅馬艦隊裡的標準船型之一，這是羅馬海軍從義大利近海走向外海的第一塊拼圖。
impactEn: The consequences of this war long outlasted the campaign. For the Illyrian kingdom the loss of Pharos meant the pillar of its Adriatic position was pulled out, and though Scodra itself did not fall at once, the capital had lost its shield at sea; in 219 BC, during the Second Illyrian War, the Romans took Scodra and Rhizon and the Ardiaean kingdom was destroyed, its cities scattering to find new patrons, with the Daorsi of Dalmatia and later Gentius rising in turn. For Rome this was the first time it had left Italy, pushed its fleet into the Adriatic, and fought as an alliance: the infantry and grain of the Aetolians, Achaeans and Pergamenes proved that Rome could fight a large war through its partners without loading the citizen levy alone, and the foothold at Corcyra and Dyrrhachium, together with the bases at Issa and Pharos, gave Rome a landing place on the western Balkan shore on which the Third Macedonian War and the Greek wars of the 2nd century BC would later rest. Economically, Illyrian silver and shipbuilding timber now flowed to Rome in quantity and became a real support for her wars in Italy, Sicily and Greece. In the intellectual sense, this was the first war fought by the Romans and written down by the Romans: the historian Polybius begins his whole History with it, and the earliest work of Roman history, the Hexapterigon, grew out of it; Polybius was himself an Illyrian, and what he wrote down was not only a war but a family memory of inherited enmity. Finally, there was the transfer of naval technique: the Illyrian fast ships were absorbed by the Romans after the war and became one of the standard types of the Roman fleet, the first piece in the assembly of a navy moving from the Italian coastal waters out into the open sea.
result: 公元前228年秋，戰事以羅馬的決定性勝利收場。法拉斯的德米特里奧斯率部歸附，羅馬接管了法拉斯島（哈瓦爾）與伊薩（維斯），在沿海建立了可以長期維持的據點；伊利里亞的戰船或毀或被俘，海上活動能力大為削弱。特歐塔沒有再戰，派人赴羅馬求和；羅馬方面接受了和解，據史家記載並未索取大筆賠款，只以人質與停戰為條件。斯庫德拉與里松未被攻下——羅馬當時既缺乏攻城器具，也沒有把戰爭擴大到全境的理由；但從此伊利里亞內陸的城邦在兩面受壓，德米特里奧斯控制的法拉斯與倒向羅馬的伊薩把王國的海岸線切開。第二次伊利里亞戰爭在公元前219年爆發，德米特里奧斯反叛，羅馬再伐，攻下斯庫德拉，阿爾迪亞伊王國覆亡；羅馬把部分土地分給羅得島人與埃托利亞人，作為聯盟的酬勞。第一次伊利里亞戰爭的結果因此不是終局，而是一段長期過程的開頭：羅馬贏得了海戰與登陸，卻把更深的一層留給了後人；對特歐塔而言，海盜的年代結束了，她和後來的統治者再無法靠海路為生。
resultEn: In the autumn of 228 BC the campaign ended in a decisive Roman victory. Demetrius of Pharos came over with his men, and Rome took over the island of Pharos (Hvar) and Issa (Vis), establishing posts that could be held for years; Illyrian vessels were destroyed or captured and the capacity for activity at sea was greatly reduced. Teuta did not fight on. Envoys came to Rome to ask for terms, and the Romans accepted, taking, according to the historian, no large indemnity but asking only for hostages and a truce. Scodra and Rhizon were not taken — the Romans had neither the siege equipment nor any reason to widen the war — but from that point the inland Illyrian cities were pressed from two sides, and Pharos under Demetrius together with Issa turned to Rome cut the kingdom's coastline in two. The Second Illyrian War broke out in 219 BC, when Demetrius revolted; the Romans came again, took Scodra, and the Ardiaean kingdom went down; some of the land was handed to the Rhodians and the Aetolians as payment to her allies. The outcome of the First Illyrian War was therefore not a final settlement but the opening of a long process: Rome won the sea battle and the landing, and left the deeper layer to those who came after; for Teuta the age of piracy was over, and neither she nor her successors could live off the sea road any more.
